newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 2.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh is due in Indonesia today and tomorrow on an official visit, his first foreign trip since taking office. He is expected to discuss fishery problems etween the two countries and certain ASEAN activities. (BANGKOK POST)

- Malaysia recently met Thailand's request for information pertaining to the arrest of a Pattani United Liberation Organisation (PULO) leader suspected of masterminding several bombings in the southern provinces. Details of Samail Thanam's apprehension in Malaysia were submitted to the Thai embassy in December. Thailand has frequently asked Kuala Lumpur to confirm the arrest, saying it wants to extradite Samail. (THE NATION)

- Cabinet has been asked to approve plans to build a 3.3 billion baht nuclear research reactor. The Office of Atomic Energy for Peace, which is seeking approval, has contracted General Atomic of the United States to build the reactor. However, the contract cannot be signed because the company's quote is 2.75 billion baht above the figure aapproved by the cabinet. (BANGKOK POST)

- Thai Petrochemical Industry Plc is planning to invest $500 million to construct a cement factory in China, capable of producing two million tonnes. The company expects that cement plant to be located in Anqing city in the east of China. The provincial government has reached an agreement with the company already but is waiting for the nod from the central government in Beijing. (BUSINESS DAY)

- The Transport and Communications Ministry will conclude a long-awaited five-year corporate plan for state-owned Thai Airways International this month and submit the plan to Cabinet for approval. The plan was originally scheduled for completion in 1996, but was delayed because of the recent change of government. (THE NATION)

- The Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) forecasts intensifying competition in the oil business will force oil companies to diversify into related businesses to maintain their profitability. The company projects production totalling 14.6 billion litres next year and expects production to increase to 15.2 billion litres in 2001. (BUSINESS DAY)
